about:
Competition Specialties, Inc. operates from Auburn, Washington, where it was established in 1966. The business is organized as a limited liability company under the name Competition Specialties, LLC. No founders are identified in the available information.

The company functions as a wholesale distributor—referred to in the trade as a jobber—supplying automotive parts and accessories to the aftermarket. It carries more than 145 major product lines, including a private-label house brand (CSI), and runs four strategically located West Coast warehouses. Services include drop-ship fulfillment, secure real-time internet ordering, a 200-plus-page full-color retail catalog, and a dedicated phone sales team. Average fill rates are reported above 94 percent.

Customers are primarily jobbers and wholesale buyers in the automotive aftermarket, covering segments such as off-road, exterior, interior, towing, and adventure accessories. Brands stocked include Warn, Factor 55, Thule, Streamlight, Ram Mounts, Rockslide, and Nufilm automotive tint. The firm also hosts what it describes as the nation’s largest jobber-only trade show.

The company emphasizes aggressive pricing and unmatched service, backed by a Performance Corner marketing program and the high fill rates noted above. No specific founding mission is documented beyond the longevity of the operation.

name: Complete Medical Supply Inc
old_description: Our knowledgable sales representatives look forward to helping you!
about:
Complete Medical Supply Inc operates from Suffern, New York, where it was founded in 1988. The company functions as a health product manufacturer, importer, and master wholesaler, with a dedicated manufacturing arm known as Complete Medical Supplies Manufacturing Group.

The firm produces its own Blue Jay™ brand of healthcare products, which spans more than 14,000 items across medical, homecare, and ergonomic categories. In addition to manufacturing, it imports and distributes lines such as Obus Forme® back and neck pain solutions. Services include drop shipping with no minimum order requirements, custom assembly of college student kits for physical therapy, occupational therapy, and medical programs, and an offshore sourcing program aimed at reducing costs. Customers order through Complete-Connect™, a 24/7 online platform, and can receive local truck delivery in the company's service area.

The customer base includes professional end-users, resellers, and educational institutions. Custom kits are built to university specifications for PT, OT, nursing, and medical students. The company also offers vendor-exclusive representation agreements and provides marketing support such as custom flyer creation and product datafeeds for reseller websites.

Complete Medical Supply emphasizes its dual role as manufacturer and wholesaler, allowing it to control quality on its Blue Jay line while offering a broad imported catalog. The no-minimum drop-ship model and integrated online ordering system are positioned as ways to lower procurement overhead for healthcare providers and retailers.

about:
Components Corporation operates from Denville, New Jersey. The company was founded by Jerry B. Minter, who served as its president, and has been producing printed circuit test points for over 60 years. While the exact founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business built its early reputation on the TP Series of test points and later expanded into a broader range of wireform interconnect products.

The company designs, manufactures, and engineers precision printed circuit test points, wireform interconnect and testing devices, card edge connectors, preform jumpers, battery contacts, and related hardware. Its product portfolio includes test points (including silver-plated and color-coded versions), card edge connectors such as the DIGI-KLIP® series, PC mount wireforms, sockets, shunts, headers, fuse clips, and circuit card guides. Components Corporation also offers custom wireform manufacturing, using proprietary technology to meet specific customer requirements. The firm serves orders of any quantity, from prototype to production volumes.

Components Corporation serves customers in medical devices, security electronics, industrial electronics, military, commercial, consumer, and aerospace sectors. Its components are used in mission-critical applications across these industries. The company reaches markets through a worldwide network of certified distributors and regional manufacturing sales representatives, enabling delivery across the United States and internationally.

The company states that its differentiation lies in a "no failure" credo, a commitment to customer satisfaction, and the ability to provide custom wireform solutions tailored to unique needs. It emphasizes high-quality, innovative products and exemplary customer service as reasons clients return. All parts are manufactured to be RoHS and REACH compliant, meeting Directive 2015/863/EU and EU Regulation EC 1907/2006.

name: Composite Fabrics of America LLC
old_description: Carbon fiber and composite materials for aerospace applications
about:
Composite Fabrics of America LLC operates from Hiddenite, North Carolina, as a wholly owned subsidiary of Schneider Mills, one of the oldest and most advanced weaving mills in the United States. The company leverages that legacy to produce carbon fiber and composite reinforcing materials for demanding applications.

The firm specializes in industry-standard and custom reinforcing fabrics for aerospace composite part fabrication and repair. Its textile engineers collaborate with customers to develop custom reinforcing products that meet design-specific requirements, reduce waste, or add aesthetic appeal. A "Bill and Hold" service allows clients to lock in pricing and secure fabric availability against market fluctuations.

The company serves aerospace, automotive, infrastructure, and athletics markets. Aerospace customers include those fabricating and repairing composite parts for aircraft, space, and defense programs, supported by a quality system certified to AS9100 Rev D.

Certification to AS9100 Rev D underscores its quality system for the Aircraft, Space and Defense industry. The Schneider Mills heritage combined with the CFA team’s capabilities is cited as the foundation for its quality and innovation in composite fabric development.

about:
Computer Cable Connection, Inc. (CCC) is headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. The firm was established in 1986 as a full-service BICSI and RCDD network cable design and installation company serving private, state, and federal institutions.

The company provides structured cabling, voice and data network design and installation, rack and cabinet layout, cable management, UPS/PDU installation, fiber optic installation and repair (including fusion splicing, testing, termination, and certification), custom cable assemblies built to specified length, color, and termination, as well as specialty systems such as DAS, sound masking, medical equipment installation, audio/visual, and intercom/paging. CCC reports more than 30,000 completed projects, over 870 appointed contractors, and 26 awards won.

CCC works with private-sector businesses, state agencies, and federal government clients, with a noted focus on medical equipment installation for healthcare facilities. Its technicians are trained to BICSI standards and manufacturer specifications, and the firm emphasizes information technology consulting, system design, and integration services.

The company’s stated vision centers on building long-term partnerships, delivering on time and to specification, recognizing employees and clients as key assets, maintaining flexibility in a changing market, and establishing a reputation for quality services at fair prices.

name: Conner Industries – Lewisburg
old_description: Learn more about our sustainability initiatives and how we help our customers meet their own environmental and sustainability goals.
about:
Conner Industries operates a location in Lewisburg, Tennessee, as part of a national network that began in 1986. The company has grown to 14 facilities across the United States, providing industrial packaging and wood products from a base in the Volunteer State.

The Lewisburg site manufactures custom and standard pallets, crates, and industrial lumber, including southern yellow pine and hardwood options with heat‑treatment for export compliance. Beyond wood, the company delivers integrated multi‑material packaging solutions that combine corrugate, foam, and plastics, and it backs those products with a suite of services: packaging consultation and design, unit‑load testing through independent labs, third‑party logistics (3PL), vendor‑managed inventory, kitting, assembly, co‑locating, repackaging, and just‑in‑sequence delivery. The operation serves wholesale and bulk customers exclusively, leveraging multiple redundancies to maintain supply continuity.

Customers span energy, oil and gas; automotive; aerospace and defense; chemical and plastics; pharmaceutical, food and beverage, and consumer products; HVAC and appliance; heavy industrial, pipe, steel, and heavy equipment; agricultural, lawn and garden; logistics and transportation; and export‑compliant lumber and packaging. The company works with industrial manufacturers that need protective packaging to keep production lines moving.

Conner differentiates itself with a consultative, material‑agnostic design approach, a total‑cost methodology that reduces waste and freight expense, and a sustainability narrative that positions lumber as a carbon‑negative material. Independent package testing avoids conflicts of interest, while the nationwide footprint and backup capabilities enable rapid response to disruptions.

name: Consolidated Metco Inc
old_description: Driving the industry forward with transformative solutions since 1964
about:
Consolidated Metco Inc., doing business as ConMet, was founded in 1964 in Clackamas, Oregon, as part of Portland Freightliner, a subsidiary of Consolidated Freightways. The company became independent in 1987 before being acquired by Varlen Corp. in 1989 and later by Amsted Industries in 1999. Today it operates as a subsidiary of Amsted Industries, with its corporate headquarters in Vancouver, Washington, and a major manufacturing campus in Clackamas.

ConMet designs and manufactures wheel-end systems, structural plastic components, permanent-mold aluminum castings, and aerodynamic devices for commercial vehicles. Its processes include aluminum die casting, permanent-mold casting, CNC machining, plastic injection molding and assembly, and wheel-end foundry and machining. The company runs 13 to 16 global manufacturing locations across North America, China, and Europe, encompassing foundries, machine shops, assembly lines, and a technical center. Annual output exceeds 3 billion products, with more than 60 million hubs produced and 18 million vehicles on the road equipped with ConMet parts.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers and commercial fleets in the heavy-duty truck and trailer market, as well as the North American aftermarket. Recent customer examples include European OEMs accessing ConMet's wheel-end engineering and production at IAA, and fleets purchasing TruCast brake drums through the aftermarket network. ConMet also supports electrification initiatives through its eMobility solutions.

ConMet emphasizes collaborative design–development–testing–validation cycles, advanced automation, and sustainable manufacturing practices such as high-efficiency furnaces, heat-treat optimization, and extensive recycling. The company states its purpose is a "relentless pursuit to imagine and engineer transformative solutions that improve the success of our customers and the lives of our employees."

name: Consolidated Telcom
old_description: Consolidated is the premier provider of telecommunication services in Southwestern North Dakota since 1961. Customer service is our main priority, from customer service representatives, internet and service support, to our technicians in the field. You, our customer, are our number one priority, 24/7/365.
about:
Consolidated Telcom, headquartered in Dickinson, North Dakota, traces its roots to January 2, 1961, when the Bowman‑Slope Rural Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation and the Dunn Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation merged to form the Consolidated Telephone Cooperative. The cooperative is owned by its members—customers who use its services—and governed by an elected board of directors.

The company provides telecommunications services across southwestern North Dakota, including fiber‑to‑the‑home internet, cable television, voice, and business services such as cybersecurity and camera solutions. Since 2005 it has built a 100% fiber‑to‑the‑home network in its cooperative exchanges, serving 19 communities, and is extending fiber upgrades to its competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) territory in Dickinson, Belfield, and Gladstone. Operations also include a CATV system acquired in 2000 that now covers the entire cooperative service area.

Consolidated serves residential and business customers in rural and small‑town markets across southwestern North Dakota. Its customer base includes households, farms, ranches, and enterprises such as Dickinson State University, which became its first CLEC client in 1998. The cooperative model aims to deliver urban‑level services at affordable rates to communities that larger carriers often overlook.

Founded to bring essential telephone service to areas where commercial providers found it unprofitable, the cooperative remains driven by its mission to “empower our communities by delivering advanced telecommunications products and services and building reliable, future‑ready infrastructure.” Its structure returns revenues above operating costs to members as capital credits, aligning incentives with customer needs rather than shareholder profit.

about:
Container and Packaging operates from Boise, Idaho, as a wholesale distributor of bottles, jars, closures, and packaging supplies. The company sources its inventory from a worldwide network of manufacturing partners, offering containers in plastic (including PET, HDPE, and PP), glass, metal, and post-consumer recycled (PCR) resins.

Beyond stock packaging, the company provides in-house decoration services such as screen printing, hot foil stamping, and shrink sleeves, along with custom box manufacturing, packaging design consultation, label printing, warehousing, logistics, and dedicated sourcing for custom or complex projects.

Its customer base spans food and beverage, personal care, pharmaceuticals, essential oils, nutrition and supplements, pet care, art supplies, and chemical and industrial markets. The company highlights work with small brands and startups—including Lone Star Bee Co., Amallow Skincare, and Brwnsgr Skincare—that order volumes from a handful of units up to several thousand.

Container and Packaging differentiates itself through personalized account management: representatives offer quick quote turnaround (often same-day), multiple shipping options, pre-purchase samples, and hands-on problem solving. The company encourages customers to call for custom needs, framing its team as a sourcing partner that can locate items not found in the online catalog.
